title: Generalizable Low-Resource Activity Recognition with Diverse and Discriminative Representation Learning

problem.claim: Human activity recognition requires adequate data, but labeled data is costly to collect and data from different persons exhibits distribution shifts that hinder generalization to unseen subjects.

gap.claim: HAR needs a method that addresses both low-resource data conditions and distribution shifts when applying trained models to new unseen subjects.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Diverse and Discriminative representation Learning (DDLearn) for generalizable low-resource HAR.
DDLearn combines diversity learning through a self-supervised task and diversity preservation module with discriminative representation learning through supervised contrastive learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DDLearn as a novel approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three public HAR datasets reportedly show that DDLearn outperforms state-of-the-art methods by an average accuracy improvement of 9.5% under low-resource distribution-shift scenarios.
The authors characterize the framework as generic, explainable, and flexible.
Code is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: HAR is framed as a time series classification task based on motion patterns in human sensor readings.
Low-resource data collection and person-level distribution shifts make generalization to unseen subjects difficult.
DDLearn addresses the setting by jointly learning diverse and discriminative representations using self-supervised, diversity-preserving, and supervised contrastive components.
The authors report results from three public HAR datasets, including a 9.5% average accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art methods.
The abstract reports that code is available.

source_observation.claim: The approach jointly targets feature diversity and semantic discrimination in a low-resource distribution-shift setting.

interpretation.claim: Combining augmentation or domain-diversity mechanisms with discriminative representation learning may address complementary sources of poor generalization.

application.claim: For sensor-based classification with limited labels and subject-level shifts, consider pairing diversity-oriented representation learning with supervised contrastive objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond the reported HAR datasets or to other data regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, sample sizes, label budgets, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not provide ablations, statistical uncertainty, or details of the reported accuracy comparison.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture or computational requirements.
